_search_metadata.note: Live web verification was performed for the two highest-stakes items (the retracted NSCLC trial and the withdrawn Banerji feasibility trial) and for the duplicate-publication claim, because those three determine which states (blocked_integrity, blocked_no_results, canonicalization) apply. Several literature items remain pending_manual_verification and are not cited for any claim until re-checked.

sources.title: Efficacy of homeopathic therapy in cancer treatment (Milazzo, Russell, Ernst; European Journal of Cancer 2006;42(3):282-289; DOI 10.1016/j.ejca.2005.09.025; PMID 16376071)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search: this is one systematic review, supplied twice as two publisher URLs for the same PII (ScienceDirect 'S0959804905009962' and ejcancer.com 'S0959-8049(05)00996-2' are the same identifier with punctuation stripped). Six studies met inclusion criteria (five RCTs, one non-randomized); conclusion: evidence encouraging but insufficient to support use, further research required. Canonicalized to this single record with occurrences=2; see src-ejcancer-duplicate-pointer for the second supplied URL's own entry, which resolves here.

sources.title: Homeopathic Treatment as an Add-On Therapy May Improve Quality of Life and Prolong Survival in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Prospective, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Three-Arm, Multicenter Study (Frass et al., The Oncologist, published online 2020-11-07; original PMC8108047)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search. Timeline: published online 2020-11-07. August 2022, the journal received a report from the Austrian Agency for Research Integrity alleging data falsification/manipulation; the agency's September 2022 conclusion recommended retraction. The Oncologist initially issued only an Expression of Concern despite five co-authors formally requesting withdrawal of their own authorship. The paper was formally retracted 2025-11-24 (retraction notice: PubMed PMID 41277743, academic.oup.com/oncolo/article/30/11/oyaf364). Commentary (PMC12908276 / PMID 41692741, 'Trials and tribulations of responsible people trying to uphold scientific standards') criticizes the retraction notice for not addressing the specific concerns raised. This source and any republication based on the same dataset are permanently ineligible to substantiate a patient claim absent a future independent integrity review establishing otherwise -- not merely 'pending', but blocked.

sources.title: Retraction of: Homeopathic Treatment as an Add-On Therapy May Improve Quality of Life and Prolong Survival in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer... (PMID 41277743)
sources.notes: The retraction notice itself, registered as its own record (distinct from the retracted article) for the integrity-surveillance trail. Used only to document the retraction, never to support any efficacy claim.

sources.title: The Banerji Protocol for Advanced Breast Cancer -- Feasibility Study (Meir Medical Center; PI Moshe Frenkel, MD)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live ClinicalTrials.gov search. Overall status: WITHDRAWN, reason 'not able to recruit patients'; status verified 2019-08; study started 2014-08; no results posted. A withdrawn trial with no results is not efficacy evidence. Note: PI Moshe Frenkel is also a repeatedly-cited review author in the local APHA handout -- see source-assessment.md's investigator-concentration finding.

sources.title: Thangapazham et al. -- negative in-vitro study of homeopathic preparations against prostate/breast cancer cell lines (PMID 17101765)
sources.notes: Reported no measurable effect on cell growth or tested gene expression for Conium, Sabal, Thuja, Asterias, Phytolacca, and Carcinosin preparations.
